DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 115 s. 2021 17 September 2021 MR. VALENTINO DOMIN NAIN Sunshine Sand and Gravel Quarrying Purok 5A Katangawan General Santos City Dear Mr. Nain: This has reference to your letter dated 20 July 2021 requesting for the Department's opinion on the following issues, quoted herein in toto: ii. Is the council of Barangay Katangawan allowed to get my extracted material on the premise that I have extracted those from a government property which is the river? Should the council of Barangay Katangawan instead secure a Government Gratuitous Permit instead of asking the quarry operators for an unlimited supply of sand and gravel to answer its need of filling materials? Is the action of Barangay Katangawan to close and cancel my Permit to quarry legal under the circumstances? On the first query and second query, if you consented or allowed the Sangguniang Barangay of Katangawan to get the extracted materials, then the same may be allowed. However, you cannot be forced to give or donate the extracted material even if those are from government property considering that all local government units are already entitled to their share from the mineral agreement pursuant to Section 82 of the Philippine Mining Act of 1995, as it provides: "Section 82. Allocation of Government Share - The Government share as referred to in the preceding sections shall be shared and allocated in accordance with Sections 290 and 292 of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991. In case the development and utilization of mineral resources is undertaken by a government-owned or -controlled corporation, the sharing and allocation shall be in accordance with Sections 291 and 292 of the said Code." (Emphasis ours) Furthermore, Sections 292 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) provides that the allocative share for barangay from mining taxes, royalties, forestry and fishery charges, and such other taxes, fees, or charges, including related surcharges, interests, or fines, and from its share in any co-production, joint venture or production "Matlno, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

sharing agreement in the utilization and development of the national wealth within their territorial jurisdiction that is collected by national government is thirty-five percent (35%). Moreover, if government entity is in need of a quarry pursuant to its imperious needs, the Local Government Units (LGUs) are not precluded to secure a Government Gratuitous Permit pursuant to Section 73 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Philippine Mining Act or the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Administrative Order No. 2010-211, viz: "Section 73. Gratuitous Permits — Any Government entity/ instrumentality in need of quarry, sand and gravel or loose/ unconsolidated materials in the construction of building(s) and/ or infrastructure for public use or other purposes may apply for a Government Gratuitous Permit (MGB Form No. 8-3B) with the Provincial Governor/City Mayor through the Provincial/City Mining Regulatory Board for a period coterminous with the construction stage of the project but not to exceed one (1) year in public/private land(s) covering an area of not more than two (2) hectares. The applicant shall submit a project proposal stating where the materials to be taken shall be used and the estimated volume needed." (Emphasis ours) On the last query on the grounds for cancellation of Permit to Quarry, we find Section 100 of DENR Administrative Order No. 2010-21 enlightening, thus: "Section 100. Cancellation/Revocation/Termination of a Quarry/Sand and Gravel/Gratuitous/Guano/ Gemstone Gathering Permit — The Quarry/Sand and Gravel/Gratuitous/ Guano/ Gemstone Gathering Permit may be canceled/revoked/terminated, after due process, by the Regional Director/ProvinciaI Governor/City Mayor concerned based on the following grounds: a. b. c. d. e. f. Failure to comply with the terms and conditions of the Permit and ECC, if applicable; Violation of any provision of the Act and these implementing rules and regulations; Failure to pay the excise tax for two (2) consecutive years; Any misrepresentation in any statement made in the application or those made later in support thereof; If the commodity stipulated in the Permit has been exhausted before the expiry date thereof; and When national interest and public welfare so require or for environmental protection or ecological reasons. Upon cancellation of the Permit, the said areas shall automatically be reverted back to its original status. 1 Entitled, 'Providing for a Consolidated Department of Environment and Natural Resources Administrative Order for the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 7942, othemise known as "The Philippine Mining Act of 1995" dated 28 June 2010" Page 2 of 3

This Department is of the view that the cancellation or revocation of the Gathering Permit is within the province of the Local Chief Executive or any authority who legally issued the same. Provided that such cancellation or revocation is within the exclusive grounds enumerated above and in compliance with the requirement of due process. Lastly, this Department notes the Barangay Resolution No. 153 Series of 2021, requesting City Mayor Ronnel C. Rivera to revoke/cancel the business permit of Sunshine Sand and Gravel owned by you. With this, unless there exists a valid ground/s for the cancellation or revocation of the business permit, the City Mayor has the power to do so pursuant to Section 455(b)(3)(iv) of the LGC2. Be that as it may, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any other contrary opinion of more competent authorities. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concern. Thank you. Very truly yours, UTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MAR AN e eta for Local Government LLLS/RPB/LRALLD/rrao/OUSLG-anor Copv fumished : DIR.
